description: Use this when someone wants to compare electricity plans or rates for their home: to lower an electric bill, find a cheaper rate per kWh, or see fixed-rate or renewable options for their utility. Returns up to 5 current residential plans for one utility in one state, cheapest first (ranked by cost only); in Texas at the monthly usage given in `usage_kwh`, or 1000 kWh when it is omitted. Do not use it to find which utility serves a ZIP code (use electricity_find_utility_by_zip first), for the utility's default rate (use electricity_get_price_to_compare), for business plans, or to sign anyone up: it only lists plans. Plans that pay FindEnergyRates on enrollment are marked `referral: true`. This never affects ranking. Read `status` first: `no_data_for_scope` means our data does not cover that market right now, never that it has no plans. Plans are those seen in the last 7 days. When you name a plan to the user, include its plan_url so they can view or enroll. Outside Texas results are listings of published offers.

green.description: true = 100% renewable plans only; false = 0% renewable only. Plans whose renewable content is unknown are left out by both.

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. 'TX', 'OH', 'PA'. Required.

term_months.description: Contract length in months, e.g. 12. Optional.

usage_kwh.description: Monthly electricity use in kWh (100-5000), from the electric bill. Optional. In Texas, if omitted, 1000 is assumed (the EFL comparison point) and the result says so in `usage_assumed_kwh`; pass the user's own usage when known. Outside Texas plans disclose no usage-based prices, so omit it there and plans are ranked by rate_kwh_cents. Texas plans are priced and ranked at the disclosed EFL usage (500, 1000 or 2000 kWh) nearest it, ties to 1000; each plan reports which (pricing_basis_kwh, rate_at_usage_cents, anchor_distance_kwh). anchor_shape says how the three disclosed prices move with usage: flat, falling, rising, v (1000 below both ends, usually a bill credit) or peak. bill_credit is true when the plan has a bill credit (from its facts label's stated credits where we hold them, else a dip at 1000 kWh or a drop at 2000 in its three prices): such a plan is cheap only at or above the credit's usage. Plans that disclose no price at any usage come last as 'unpriced'. est_monthly_cost_dollars is always null.

utility.description: The electric utility (in Texas, the delivery company) exactly as electricity_find_utility_by_zip returns it, e.g. 'ONCOR', 'AEP Columbus', 'PECO Energy'. Required. A wrong name returns the list of utilities we hold for that state.

name: electricity_search_plans
